---
title: Using it in a book
---

## Install it

In your Quarto book or website project, install a tagged release:

```bash
quarto add UBC-MDS/ubc-quarto-brand@v0.1.0
```

Quarto copies the extension into `_extensions/UBC-MDS/ubc/`.
Commit that folder: your book keeps exactly this version until you update it.

## Use the format

In your `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
format: ubc-html
```

That one line brings the theme, the listing labels, the callouts and the quizzes.
The brand's colours, fonts and dark-mode toggle reach every HTML page as soon as the extension
is installed, even one with a plain `format: html`.
The rest needs `ubc-html`, readable tab titles in dark mode included:
a plain `format: html` page paints the active tab's title in the page's own navy.

## Update it

```bash
quarto update UBC-MDS/ubc-quarto-brand@v0.2.0
```

Do it in a pull request of its own, so the preview shows what changed before you merge.
The [changelog](../CHANGELOG.md) lists what each release changed.

## Turn on the MDS logo

The MDS logo ships with the extension but is not shown unless you ask for it.
In a book:

```yaml
book:
  sidebar:
    logo: _extensions/UBC-MDS/ubc/MDSlogo.png
    logo-alt: "MDS logo"
```

In a website, the same two keys go under `website: sidebar:`, or under `website: navbar:` for a logo in the navbar.

## Add your own styles

Add a theme layer of your own. Give it to both modes, as two lists:

```yaml
format:
  ubc-html:
    theme:
      light: [extra.scss]
      dark: [extra.scss]
```

Your layer comes after the extension's, so a rule of yours wins over one of the extension's
with an equally specific selector.
The extension's dark-mode rules start with `body.quarto-dark`; start yours the same way to override them.
In your layer's `/*-- scss:rules --*/` section the brand's colours are available as `$brand-<name>`,
for example `$brand-ubc-blue`.
Its `/*-- scss:defaults --*/` section can set Bootstrap's and Quarto's Sass variables,
such as `$callout-color-note`, and they win over the extension's in both modes,
except `$body-emphasis-color`, which DSCI 521's `styles-dark.scss` sets for dark mode;
use literal hex there, because the `$brand-*` names do not exist yet when defaults are read.
A single list, `theme: [extra.scss]`, makes Quarto stop with an error.

## Add or recolour a callout type

Add `custom-callout:` keys to your `_quarto.yml`. They merge with the extension's:
a new type is added, and a type the extension already has takes the keys you give it.
This adds a `lab` type and recolours `activity`:

```yaml
custom-callout:
  lab:
    title: "Lab"
    icon: true
    icon-symbol: "fa-flask"
    color: "#A6192E"
  activity:
    color: "#0077C8"
```

The colour must be a literal hex, because this YAML cannot read the brand's Sass.
custom-callout uses it for the callout's border and fill in light mode, and nothing else.
The icon's colour and the dark-mode colours come from theme rules:
the extension has them for its own four types,
so a type you add gets an uncoloured icon and the same border on the dark page,
and a type you recolour keeps the extension's icon colour and dark-mode border.
Add the rules to your own layer (see above),
taking each dark colour from the light one's pair in the table below:

```scss
/*-- scss:rules --*/

div.callout-lab .callout-icon::before {
  margin-right: 0.4em; /* only for a new type: the extension spaces its own */
  color: $brand-alert-red;
}

div.callout-activity .callout-icon::before {
  color: $brand-ubc-blue-mid;
}

body.quarto-dark {
  div.callout-lab.callout {
    border-left-color: $brand-alert-red-light;
  }

  div.callout-lab .callout-icon::before {
    color: $brand-alert-red-light;
  }

  div.callout-activity.callout {
    border-left-color: $brand-ubc-blue-bright;
  }

  div.callout-activity .callout-icon::before {
    color: $brand-ubc-blue-bright;
  }
}
```

| Light mode | Hex | Its dark-mode pair | Hex |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ubc-blue` | `#002145` | `ubc-blue-pale` | `#97D4E9` |
| `ubc-blue-deep` | `#0055B7` | `ubc-blue-light` | `#40B4E5` |
| `ubc-blue-mid` | `#0077C8` | `ubc-blue-bright` | `#00A7E1` |
| `ubc-gold-dark` | `#8A6D2B` | `ubc-gold` | `#A89565` |
| `mds-green` | `#1C5F2E` | `mds-green-light` | `#88D4AB` |
| `alert-red` | `#A6192E` | `alert-red-light` | `#F08080` |

The [Callouts](callouts.qmd) page shows every type the extension defines.

## What you cannot change

You cannot replace part of the brand.
A `_brand.yml` of your own is ignored, because the extension's brand takes its place.
A top-level `brand:` key replaces the whole brand:
written inline, it stops the render with an undefined `$brand-*` variable,
and only `brand:` pointing at a complete copy of the extension's `brand.yml` renders.
To change how things look, add a theme layer instead.

## Executed code and quizzes

Executed R and Python cells need nothing from the extension.
Quizzes are written in a `quizdown` code block;
the [conventions page](book-conventions.qmd) shows each kind.
